chapter_theme: The single song at Thiruppadikkarai (திருப்படிக்கரை): the poet asks to turn from courtesans who strip a man's wealth to praising the shrine and singing Murugan's Thiruppugazh; the praise is Rama's war and the father who praises Murugan's Tamil.

787.reading: The poet describes women who come close, smile softly, line their eyes, call, say sweet things, loosen the silk bought by selling a half-panam, embrace, give their lips and melt a man with love until they have taken his wealth without limit, and asks whether, without delusion for them in his heart, he will praise the shrine of Seyppathi and sing Murugan's Thiruppugazh. The praise tells of Rama with the army of monkeys, the dammed sea and the arrow that shattered the demons, as uncle, and names Murugan the one in the three Tamils whom his father praises, at Thiruppadikkarai.
787.nuance: மட்டறப் பொருட் பறிப்பவர், those who pluck wealth without measure, names the courtesans. உனைத் திருப்புகழ்ப் பகர்வேனோ: the poet names his own work as the alternative to the women, as in 263. செய்ப்பதித் தலம் is probably the shrine itself, or Vayalur, whose name is the same; the reading leaves it open.
